name: Darjeeling Tea
description: Darjeeling Tea is a tea grown in the Darjeeling district of West Bengal. It is light-colored and has a distinctive muscatel flavor and aroma. The first GI tag granted in India.
note: First Geographical Indication registered in India

name: Kancheepuram Silk
applicant: Silk Weavers Service Co-operative Society Ltd
description: Kancheepuram silk sarees are known for their distinctive heavy borders and richness of design. Made from pure mulberry silk and zari threads, each saree takes weeks to complete.
note: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage candidate

name: Banarasi Brocades & Sarees
description: Banarasi sarees are made of finely woven silk and decorated with intricate gold and silver zari embroidery. Centuries-old weaving tradition of Varanasi known worldwide.
note: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity

name: Pashmina
description: Pashmina is a fine type of cashmere wool from the Changthangi goat of Ladakh. Handspun and hand-woven Pashmina shawls are renowned worldwide for their softness and warmth.
note: Derived from Persian word for soft gold

name: Phulkari
applicant: Punjab State Co-operative Handloom & Handicrafts Corporation
description: Phulkari literally means flower work. Traditional embroidery of Punjab on coarse cotton fabric with colorful silk thread using a darning stitch creating floral patterns.
note: Traditional craft of rural Punjab women

name: Madhubani Paintings
description: Madhubani painting or Mithila painting is a style of Indian painting practised in the Mithila region. Characterised by geometric patterns and vivid colours depicting nature and mythology.
note: Practiced by women of the Mithila region for centuries

name: Pochampally Ikat
description: Pochampally Ikat is a type of silk textile known for its geometric patterns done in a double ikat style. Originates from Bhoodan Pochampally village, Telangana.
note: Village known as Silk City of India

name: Pattachitra
applicant: Odisha Khadi and Village Industries Board
description: Pattachitra is a traditional cloth-based scroll painting from Odisha. Known for intricate details, mythological narratives and use of natural colors extracted from plants and minerals.
note: One of the oldest art forms of Odisha

name: Kondapalli Toys
description: Kondapalli Toys are wooden toys from Kondapalli village in Andhra Pradesh. Made from white sycamore wood, known for bright colors and traditional Indian themes.
note: 400-year-old toy making tradition

name: Warli Art
applicant: Maharashtra Small Scale Industries Dev Corp
description: Warli painting is a style of tribal art created by the Warli people of Maharashtra. Uses simple geometric shapes depicting nature, community and daily life in white on earth-toned background.
note: Geometric style of tribal art dating to 2500 BCE

name: Channapatna Toys & Dolls
description: Channapatna toys are wooden toys and dolls from Karnataka, made from ivory wood and lacquered with non-toxic vegetable dyes. Known for smooth texture and bright natural colors.
note: Known as toy town of Karnataka

name: Kashmiri Kani Shawl
description: Kani shawls are special shawls woven with wooden spools called kani. The intricate patterns are produced by intermeshing colored threads using bamboo/wooden skewers.
note: Each shawl takes 6-18 months to weave

name: Aranmula Kannadi
applicant: Aranmula Handloom and Handicrafts Weavers & Arts Co-op
description: Aranmula Kannadi is a unique metal mirror from Aranmula, Kerala, made using a special bronze alloy. The alloy composition is a family secret passed through generations.
note: Only front-surface metal mirror in the world

name: Bidriware
description: Bidriware is a metalwork craft from Bidar, Karnataka involving casting zinc-copper alloy articles, inlaying with silver, and oxidizing with special soil to achieve a black background.
note: 500-year-old craft from Bahmani Sultanate era

name: Lucknow Chikankari
applicant: UP Handloom and Textile Dev Corporation
description: Chikankari is a delicate traditionally hand-embroidered textile from Lucknow. The craft involves intricate needlework with white thread on white or pastel fabric creating shadow patterns.
note: Introduced in India by Mughal Empress Noor Jahan

name: Blue Pottery of Jaipur
description: Blue Pottery of Jaipur is unique as it is not clay-based. Made from quartz, raw glaze and sodium sulphate, decorated with blue and green colors derived from copper and cobalt oxide.
note: Technique brought by Mughals from Persia

name: Kashmiri Sozni Embroidery
description: Sozni embroidery is extremely fine needlework done on Pashmina shawls from Kashmir. The needle work is so fine that it creates patterns visible from both sides of the fabric.
note: Finest needlework in the world - both sides identical

name: Chettinad Cotton Textiles
applicant: Tamil Nadu Handloom Weavers Co-operative Society
description: Chettinad cotton textiles are traditional handwoven fabrics from the Chettinad region of Tamil Nadu. Known for their bold check and stripe patterns in predominantly earth tones.
note: Traditional attire of Chettiar community

name: Kutch Embroidery
applicant: Gujarat State Handicrafts and Handloom Dev Corporation
description: Kutch embroidery is a traditional craft of the Kutch district known for vibrant colors, intricate patterns and use of mirrors in the needlework by different tribal communities.
note: Multiple styles from different tribal communities

name: Mysore Agarbathi
description: Mysore Agarbathi refers to incense sticks produced in the Mysore region. The unique fragrance comes from specific sandalwood and natural ingredients available in the Mysore region.
note: Mysore produces 85% of India's agarbathis

name: Dhokra Metal Craft
description: Dhokra is a non-ferrous metal casting using the lost-wax casting technique. One of the oldest known methods dating to 4000 years. Every Dhokra piece is unique.
note: 4000-year-old non-ferrous metal casting technique

name: Goan Feni
description: Feni is a type of spirit produced from cashew apples in Goa. Distilled twice using traditional clay pots and copper vessels, giving it a unique character and local flavor.
note: Goa Heritage Liquor - exclusive Indian GI spirit

name: Thanjavur Painting
description: Thanjavur painting is a classical South Indian painting style from Thanjavur. Known for surface richness, vivid colors and compact composition embellished with gold foil and semi-precious stones.
note: 16th-century art form from Nayak dynasty

name: Meenakari Jewellery of Jaipur
description: Meenakari is the art of painting and colouring the surfaces of metals by fusing brilliant colours into intricately detailed enamel. The Jaipur style uses a gold base and vivid colors.
note: Introduced in India by Raja Man Singh I from Lahore

name: Assam Muga Silk
applicant: Assam State Federation of Handloom Weavers
description: Muga silk is the product of the Antheraea assamensis silkworm, endemic to Assam. It is the only silk in the world that improves with washing, becoming more lustrous over time.
note: World's only natural golden silk; gets shinier with washing

name: Kullu Shawl
description: Kullu Shawls are handwoven shawls from the Kullu Valley of Himachal Pradesh. Known for distinctive geometric patterns, bright colors and use of local Angora and Merino wool.
note: Traditional shawl from the Valley of the Gods

name: Bagh Print
description: Bagh print is a traditional hand block-printing technique from the Bagh village in MP. Uses natural and organic colors derived from minerals and vegetables applied on cotton/silk fabric.
note: Named after Bagh river; uses gobar and alizarin dyes

name: Sanganer Printed Textiles
description: Sanganer is famous for its block-printed textiles using wooden hand-carved blocks. The prints feature intricate floral and geometric patterns on light muslin or cotton fabric.
note: Named after Sanganer town near Jaipur

name: Lepcha Woven Fabric
description: Lepcha woven fabric is a traditional textile of the Lepcha people of Sikkim. Features intricate geometric motifs and is traditionally woven on a backstrap loom using silk and cotton threads.
note: Ancient weaving tradition of Lepcha tribe

name: Naga Handloom Products
description: Naga Handloom refers to traditional textiles woven by various Naga tribes on traditional back-strap looms. Each tribe has distinct motifs and color combinations representing their identity.
note: Each of 16 major Naga tribes has unique motifs

name: Manipuri Shawls
applicant: Manipur State Handloom & Handicrafts Dev Corporation
description: Manipuri Shawls are handwoven shawls from Manipur made using traditional pit loom and hand loom. Known for unique designs representing the rich cultural heritage of Manipur.
note: Woven by Manipuri women as cultural expression

name: Odisha Ikat
applicant: Odisha State Handloom Weavers Cooperative Society
description: Odisha Ikat, also known as Bandha, is an ancient tie-and-dye technique producing intricate patterns. Complex geometric motifs are produced by tie-dyeing yarn prior to weaving.
note: One of only three places in world practicing double ikat

name: Surat Zari Craft
description: Surat Zari Craft refers to intricate metallic thread embroidery using gold and silver threads. Surat has been the center of zari manufacturing in India for centuries.
note: Surat zari industry dates to Mughal era

name: Tanjore Art Plates
description: Tanjore Art Plates are decorative plates crafted using repoussé - metal shaped by hammering from the reverse side. Typically made from brass or copper with fine relief work.
note: Ancient metal-relief craft from Chola period

name: Jodhpuri Mojari
description: Mojari are traditional handcrafted footwear from Rajasthan. Made from quality leather and embellished with embroidery, mirrors and metal work, they are both functional and artistic.
note: Traditional royal footwear of Rajputana

name: Assam Tea
description: Assam tea is a black tea known for its strong, malty flavor and bright color. Produced largely on flood plains of the Brahmaputra river in Assam.
note: World's largest tea-growing region

name: Pipli Applique Work
applicant: Odisha Khadi and Village Industries Board
description: Pipli applique is the art of cutting and sewing pieces of fabric onto a larger surface to create decorative designs. The town of Pipli is known for brightly colored parasols for the Puri Jagannath Temple.
note: Used for Jagannath Temple chariot decoration for centuries

name: Coorg Coffee
description: Coorg (Kodagu) produces some of India's finest Arabica and Robusta coffee. The unique altitude of 900-1700m and rich soil in the Western Ghats gives Coorg coffee its distinctive flavor.
note: Coorg is called Scotland of India for its coffee estates

name: Tripuri Rignai and Risa
applicant: Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council
description: Rignai and Risa are traditional dress fabrics of the Tripuri community. Rignai is the lower garment and Risa is the upper garment worn by Tripuri women, featuring distinctive geometric motifs.
note: Sacred fabric worn during Garia Puja festival

name: Nirmal Paintings
applicant: Telangana State Handloom & Textile Dev Corporation
description: Nirmal paintings are made on a wooden base using a technique similar to egg tempera. Named after Nirmal town in Telangana, known for their distinctive golden background and vibrant colors.
note: 600-year-old painting tradition using wood and natural colors

name: Ladakh Thanka Painting
description: Thanka (Thangka) paintings are Buddhist devotional paintings on cotton or silk. Used as aids for meditation and teaching tools, they depict Buddhist deities and mandala patterns.
note: Each Thanka requires months of painstaking work

name: Mangalgiri Cotton Saree
description: Mangalgiri sarees are handloom sarees from Mangalgiri town in Andhra Pradesh. Known for distinctive nizam border and extra weft pattern on the border using zari or gold threads.
note: Traditional saree for Andhra festive occasions

name: Udaipur Koftgari
description: Koftgari is the art of inlaying gold and silver wire into iron or steel creating intricate designs. The Udaipur Koftgari tradition has been nurtured by royal patronage for centuries.
note: Originally used to decorate swords and daggers for royalty

name: Naga Morich Ghost Pepper
description: Bhut Jolokia (Ghost Pepper) is an interspecific hybrid chili pepper from Northeast India. It held the Guinness World Record as the world's hottest pepper from 2007 to 2011.
note: Former world's hottest pepper - Guinness Record 2007-2011

name: Mysore Silk
description: Mysore Silk is produced by the Karnataka Silk Industries Corporation and is known for its pure zari border and real gold zari work. The silk production process is unique from spinning to dyeing.
note: Mysore Silk has won National Award multiple times

name: Gwalior Dhurrie
applicant: MP Khadi and Village Industries Board
description: Gwalior Dhurrie is a flat-woven cotton rug with intricate geometric patterns. The prison labor tradition of weaving these rugs in Gwalior Fort gave birth to the commercial craft industry.
note: Tradition started in Gwalior Fort prison workshops

name: Attapady Valley Honey
description: Attapady Valley Honey is produced by the indigenous Irula, Kurumba and Muduga tribal communities from wild bee colonies in silent valley forests. Raw, unprocessed and rich in medicinal properties.
note: Produced by three indigenous tribes of Silent Valley

name: Cane and Bamboo Craft of Assam
applicant: Assam Bamboo and Cane Dev Corp
description: Assam is rich in bamboo and cane varieties. The traditional craft of making baskets, mats, furniture and decorative articles from cane and bamboo has been practiced by local communities for centuries.
note: Assam has over 58 bamboo species and 10 cane species

name: Lohari Brass Craft
description: The Lohari brass craft from Jharkhand is a traditional tribal craft of brass and bell metal casting. The Lohar community creates intricate figurines, household items and ritual objects.
note: Lohar tribe maintains this craft as hereditary tradition

name: Meghalaya Khasi Shawl
applicant: Meghalaya State Handloom and Handicraft Council
description: The Khasi Shawl is a traditional wrap woven by Khasi women of Meghalaya. Made using the traditional back-strap loom (ryndia), the shawls feature distinctive patterns specific to each Khasi clan.
note: Each Khasi clan weaves distinct patterns as identity markers

name: Idu Mishmi Textiles
applicant: Idu Mishmi Cultural and Literary Society
description: Traditional geometric hand-woven textiles of the Idu Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, distinguished by intricate diamond patterns, nettle and cotton fibers, and natural dyes.
note: Sacred tribal weaving technique passed across generations

name: Panipat Punja Dhurries
description: Heavy cotton and wool flat-woven floor rugs crafted using the heavy iron pronged tool called Punja. Celebrated for geometric motifs and timeless durability.
note: Historic textile cluster of Haryana

name: Tawlhlohpuan Weave
description: A sacred, prestigious Mizo fabric historically awarded only to warriors of outstanding courage. Hand-woven on loin looms with warp-faced stripes in red, yellow, and black.
note: Warriors cloak of honor in Mizo culture

name: Thulma Woolen Blankets
description: Hand-woven thick blankets made from indigenous Bhotiya sheep wool in high Himalayan valleys. Brushed with natural thistle combs to create a luxuriant, weather-insulating pile.
note: Woven in high-altitude Himalayan settlements
